metadata.methods_description: Each trial began with a 3 s fixation cross, followed by a 4 s visual cue and 3 s of a gray ready screen to eliminate afterimages. Participants then performed the imagined movement for 5 s. Each of the three sessions comprised 40 trials with four motor imagery tasks in random order.

citation_details.title: GeoNIRS: Geometry-Aware Pretraining for Heterogeneous fNIRS Representation Learning
citation_details.author: Zongsheng Li, Shengyuan Zhu, Zimo Zhang, Hanyao Li, Shengming Wang, Quanying Liu
citation_details.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets. We introduce GeoNIRS, a geometry-aware framework that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts. GeoNIRS compresses variable-size channel sets into a fixed-size latent representation and employs bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction with contiguous temporal masking. GeoNIRS-base is pretrained on eight heterogeneous datasets, while GeoNIRS-large scales to 22 datasets. Neither downstream data nor labels are used during pretraining, enabling evaluation under a strict cross-task setting.
